Proven risk: `src/click/core.py` is the main coupling hub for parsing, parameter sourcing, invocation, and completion handoff. Additional risk hypothesis: platform-specific console and completion behavior likely hides edge cases outside the Linux/macOS path covered here.

task_results.notes: Realistic flow explained: `setup_panic!()` in user code expands to `setup_panic(|| metadata!())` from `src/lib.rs`. That registers a panic hook in `src/panic.rs`; on panic, the hook builds `Report::with_panic`, persists it unless running in CI, and then prints the human-facing message. The integration fixture under `tests/single-panic` proves the release, debug, and CI branches of that flow.

The hook closure uses `panic::set_hook`, `Report::with_panic`, `report.persist()`, and `print_msg` in `src/panic.rs` (lines 20-33).
Crash reports are assembled in `src/report.rs` via `Report::with_panic`, `serialize`, and `persist` (lines 68, 98, 103).
Observable stderr/file behavior is asserted in `tests/single-panic/tests/integration.rs` (release at line 3, release_with_ci at line 114, debug at line 170).

task_results.notes: Symptom chosen: adding a nested group below `@click.group(chain=True)` raises a `RuntimeError` during registration instead of allowing the chain to run. Most likely fault boundary is `_check_nested_chain` in `src/click/core.py`, not the downstream invocation loop. Alternative theory: even if registration passed, `Group.invoke` would fail to resolve nested chained contexts; I kept that theory alive until runtime verification because the guard might have been masking a deeper parser limitation.
evidence: The failing symptom is captured by `test_group_chaining` in `tests/test_chain.py` (line 221 before the patch).
The failure reproduced with `uv run -m pytest tests/test_chain.py -k group_chaining --runxfail -vv`, raising from `_check_nested_chain` in `src/click/core.py`.
`_check_nested_chain` was referenced both during command registration and command collection lookup in `src/click/core.py` (lines 1657 and 2029 before the patch).
Next verification step named and executed: rerun the targeted test with `--runxfail` to see the real traceback instead of the xfail wrapper.

task_results.patch_summary: Fixed the chained nested-group regression by removing the `_check_nested_chain` guard that was blocking registration and lookup of groups under `chain=True`, then converted the existing xfail into a normal passing regression test.
task_results.notes: I treated the existing xfail as the seeded bug because it described a reproducible failure in the shipped behavior. The key observation was that bypassing the guard manually let `Group.invoke` already handle the nested chain correctly, so the fix stayed very narrow.
evidence: Root cause was `_check_nested_chain` in `src/click/core.py`, which raised before the chain could run.

A direct runtime experiment that bypassed `add_command` showed the nested chain already executed successfully (`cli=`, `l1a=`, `l2a=`, `l1b=`), so the guard was the fault boundary rather than the invocation loop.
The xfail marker was removed from `tests/test_chain.py::test_group_chaining` and the targeted chain file passed (`16 passed`).
Neighboring command tests also passed after the fix (`82 passed` in `tests/test_commands.py`).

task_results.notes: Bounded refactor target: split `pLimit` into (1) option normalization/validation and (2) queue scheduling helpers without changing behavior. tests_or_commands_run: rg -n 'lazy loading|lazy load' README.md docs/index.rst docs/complex.md src/click/core.py
task_results.notes: I found mild docs drift / overstatement. `README.md` and `docs/index.rst` say Click 'supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime', but the built-in `Group.get_command` implementation is just a direct dictionary lookup. The detailed docs in `docs/complex.md` show that lazy loading is achieved by subclassing `Group` and overriding `get_command`, not by a built-in switch. I did not patch docs because this task only asked for drift detection.
evidence: Claim source: `README.md` line 18 and `docs/index.rst` line 23 both advertise lazy loading support.
Code truth: built-in `Group.get_command` in `src/click/core.py` (lines 1792-1796) only returns `self.commands.get(cmd_name)`.
Detailed docs clarify the real mechanism: `docs/complex.md` line 227 says a `Group` subclass can implement a lazy loader by taking over `Group.get_command`.
Conclusion: the docs are directionally true at the ecosystem level, but the top-level claim overstates what the core `Group` does out of the box.
